reduction: n = water.json's n (IAPWS R9-97's since R08.T5.h) plus Quan and Fry's salinity terms, (n₁ + n₂T + n₃T²)S + n₆S ÷ λ at practical salinity S = 35 (PSS-78, dimensionless; the Web Book gives Quan and Fry's S in PSU) and T = 25 °C: +0.00672 at 380 nm, +0.00639 at 550 nm and +0.00618 at 780 nm, to six significant figures. Quan and Fry fitted Austin and Halikas 1976's data from 400–700 nm (the Web Book), relative to air, so their salinity terms alone are added to water.json's own n rather than their equation taken whole: the two files differ by Quan and Fry's salinity effect, and this one follows water.json's n should it change. k = water.json's: sea salts leave pure water's visible absorption unchanged within measurement (Röttgers, McKee and Utschig 2014, Opt. Express 22, 25093, DOI 10.1364/OE.22.025093: the salinity coefficient not significantly different from zero below 500 nm, and −0.18% to +0.04% per g L⁻¹ over 400–2,660 nm); their absorption lies in the ultraviolet. Seawater's molecular scattering is not in the file
